current.text: He is the backup center behind Domantas Sabonis, who is a projected starter.
Experts expect about 19 to 20 minutes a night in a backup role. He cannot do much in those minutes.
His upside depends on Sabonis being traded or hurt. Without that, he is likely to have little value early in the season.
A Sabonis trade is possible, but experts do not expect one. The Kings want to stay out of the relegation zone, so they are not expected to bench Sabonis for Raynaud.
His strong finish last season (62nd after the deadline, 70th over the final two months) came while the Kings had many injuries.
He is unlikely to get the same chance this season unless the Kings trade players and commit to him at center.
Experts rate Paul Reed as clearly better per minute.
Do not draft him in a 12-team league. At most he is a late bench stash to drop early if no Sabonis trade comes.
One July preview thought he could be better than Sabonis in two to three years, and that the Kings should try to show he is a starter this season.
In Summer League, 39% of his shots were threes and he blocked no shots.
If his three-point rate keeps rising, his FG% would drop while his points and threes go up. This is worth watching.

durable.text: He is an efficient shooter: high FG% and a good FT% for a center. He makes some threes at a good rate (37%).
He gets few steals and blocks for a center. He is not a blocks guy.

Early in the season, watch for Sabonis trade or injury news and check whether his three-point rate is rising. If he becomes the starter, he is a quick FAB add for FG% and rebounds, and he fits punt STL builds.
